name: High Camp
tagline: Acclimatise, pack and turn around on time
about: High Camp plans alpine and expedition climbs: acclimatisation schedules built from the altitude profile, gear lists by route grade and season, weather-window and turnaround decisions, rope and glacier skills refreshers, and a plain guide to altitude illness.
persona: You are a mountain guide: methodical, safety-first, and clear that the summit is optional and coming home is not.

onboarding.title: Climb high, come home
onboarding.subtitle: Your experience and objectives calibrate the plans.
bullets: Acclimatisation schedules from the altitude profile
Gear lists by grade and season

tools.title: Acclimatisation plan
tools.subtitle: Sleep low, climb high, on paper

inputs.label: Altitude profile
inputs.placeholder: fly to Lukla 2,860 m, trek to Khare 5,045 m, summit 6,476 m

inputs.label: Altitude history
inputs.placeholder: mild headache at 4,500 m last time, fine after a rest day

tools.prompt: Build an acclimatisation schedule for {alt} in {days} days given history: {history}. A table (Day | Sleep altitude | High point | Gain in sleeping altitude | Purpose), steps for what to do on rest days, bullets on the rules applied (300–500 m per day above 3,000 m, a rest day every 1,000 m), and a callout on the symptoms that mean descend now.

tools.title: Gear for the route
tools.subtitle: By grade, season, style
tools.prompt: Gear list for {route}, {style}, for the profile. Sections: a checklist grouped Technical / Clothing / Footwear / Sleep & bivvy / Nav & safety / Food & water, a table of the decisions that depend on conditions (Item | Take if… | Leave if…), kv (target pack weight, approximate water and food per day), and a callout on the items whose failure would end the trip.

tools.title: Summit push window
tools.subtitle: Multi-day forecast → which day, which camps

inputs.label: Forecasts (paste 2–3 sources, several days)
inputs.placeholder: Source A: Tue wind 60 km/h at 6,000 m, Wed 30 km/h, Thu 20 km/h then snow from Fri. Source B: …

inputs.label: Camps & supplies
inputs.placeholder: BC 4,900 m, high camp 5,800 m, summit 6,476 m; 4 days food above BC, 2 gas canisters

inputs.label: Team & state
inputs.placeholder: 3 of us, one slept badly, all acclimatised to 5,400 m

tools.prompt: Choose the summit push from forecasts: {forecast}, camps and supplies: {camps}, team: {team}. Sections: kv (push day, where to sleep each night, summit start time, latest summit time, hard turnaround time, plan B if the window closes), a table (Day | Sleep at | Move | Weather risk | Turn back if…), bullets of what to reassess at each camp and checkpoint, and a callout on summit fever and how the team commits to the turnaround now.

tools.title: Skills refresher
tools.subtitle: Rope, anchors, crevasse, self-arrest
tools.prompt: Refresh {skill} for the profile level. Sections: steps in order naming the gear used at each, bullets of the common mistakes and checks, a table (Situation | Variation | Why), and a callout stating this is a refresher to practise on safe ground with a qualified instructor.

tools.title: Altitude illness guide
tools.subtitle: AMS, HAPE, HACE in plain words

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: 4,900 m, headache since evening, nausea, took a while to answer questions

tools.prompt: Assess: {symptoms}. kv (likely picture: AMS / HAPE / HACE / other, severity, the one action now), steps for the next hours (stop ascent, descend, oxygen, evacuation, when to use medication a doctor prescribed), a table (Sign | AMS | HAPE | HACE), and a callout that descent is the treatment and to call for rescue early.

disclaimer: Mountaineering is dangerous. This is general information, not medical or guiding advice; train with qualified instructors, carry rescue insurance, and descend if in doubt.
